A1.justification: Both 10-page PDFs describe the same GDNet study. All text, equations, tables and figures support reliable comparison after visual verification. Neither supplied PDF contains appendices; both end with references.

before.justification: v3 reports original GDNet evaluations on AIM 2024 and Compressed-NYU, including quantitative comparisons, qualitative outputs and ablations in Tables 1–4 and Figures 4–5.

after.justification: v4 retains these original empirical results, including benchmark comparisons and component, loss-function and attention-count ablations.

M1.justification: Sections 3.1–3.4 retain the same GDNet architecture, FGDE/DCPM components, GGE low-rank reconstruction, depth decoder and SILog training objective.

E1.justification: Both versions use the TartanAir-derived AIM 2024 Compressed Depth Upsampling dataset and synthesized Compressed-NYU, with the same downsampling, bit-depth compression and random-noise scenarios.

E2.justification: Comparator membership is identical within each experiment. Tables 1–2 retain all baseline rows, including DAS-Depth and DINOv2-ControlNet on AIM 2024 and Depth Anything, UniDepth, iDisc, AdaBins and SGNet on Compressed-NYU.

E3.justification: Section 4.1 retains the same training/test counts: 3,866/257 for AIM 2024 and 795/654 for Compressed-NYU. Data augmentation, MAE/RMSE metrics and the 400-epoch training protocol are also unchanged.

E4.justification: Section 4.4 and Tables 3–4 retain the same component and loss-function ablations and sensitivity analysis of self-attention and cross-attention counts. Figures 4–5 retain the same qualitative comparisons and error-map analyses.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-run counts, random seeds, confidence intervals, error bars or statistical significance tests. The statistical reporting practice is unchanged.

E6.justification: Tables 1–4 and Figures 4–5 are unchanged. For example, GDNet retains AIM 2024 MAE/RMSE of 0.212/0.375 in Table 1 and Compressed-NYU MAE/RMSE of 0.0322/0.0739 in Table 2.

T1.justification: Equations 1–18 and their accompanying mathematical reasoning are unchanged, including the least-squares reconstruction, QR-based basis construction, low-rank projection and SILog formulation.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction and conclusion retain the same geometry-decoupling contribution, FGDE/GGE contributions and superior-reconstruction claims. The abstract's AIM challenge first-place claim is also unchanged.

C2.justification: The explanations of RGB-based detail recovery, low-rank noise suppression and global geometric consistency remain identical, as do the interpretations of comparisons and ablations. No substantive limitations or applicability qualifications are added or removed.

D1.justification: The PyTorch/A100 implementation, Adam optimizer, batch size, learning-rate schedule and loss hyperparameters are unchanged. The abstract also retains the same code-access link and destination.

R1.justification: Section 2 and all 54 references are unchanged. No cited works or substantive statements positioning GDNet relative to prior research are added, removed or revised.

P1.justification: v4 adds 'SKL-IOTSC, CIS, University of Macau' beneath the unchanged author list and updates the arXiv version/date stamp. The scientific prose and section organization remain unchanged.

P2.justification: The added affiliation produces a small first-page title-block and spacing adjustment. Figures and tables retain their content and structure, and rendered pages 2–10 are identical.

improvement.justification: v4 supplies an institutional affiliation and updates the version/date, with minor first-page formatting changes. These editorial changes leave the paper's scientific content, evidence, explanations and reproducibility information unchanged, yielding no meaningful overall quality difference.
